content.value_statement: Detailed engineering handoffs are hard when implementers lack context. This skill turns completed designs into step-by-step plans with files, tests, commands, and checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Creates implementation plan documents from completed feature designs.
Breaks work into small tasks with specific files and tests.
Includes expected verification commands and expected results for each task.
Adds example test and implementation snippets inside the plan.
Defines execution handoff options for subagent-driven or parallel-session work.
limitations: Requires a completed design or clear feature brief before planning.
Does not inspect or validate the repository unless the agent does that separately.
Example commands in plans still need human review before execution.
Best suited for software implementation work, not general project planning.

use_cases.title: Prepare Feature Build Tasks
use_cases.description: Convert an approved product or technical design into small engineering tasks with files, tests, and verification steps.

use_cases.title: Hand Off Work to a New Contributor
use_cases.description: Create a plan that gives a developer enough context to implement a change without prior repository knowledge.

use_cases.title: Structure Test-Driven Implementation
use_cases.description: Plan a TDD workflow where each task starts with a failing test, minimal code, verification, and a commit.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning request with a completed design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for this completed design. Include files, tests, verification commands, and small tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan for a New Contributor
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a developer with little repository context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a plan for an engineer who has no codebase context. Explain the files, task order, tests, and expected outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that emphasizes test-first development.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this design into a TDD implementation plan. Each task should include a failing test, minimal implementation, verification, and commit step.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Session Execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for coordinated implementation handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detailed implementation plan with execution handoff options. Include checkpoints for subagent-driven work and a separate parallel session.

output_examples.input: A design for adding saved filters to a dashboard.
output_examples.output: A dated plan file with a goal, architecture summary, task list, exact affected files, test steps, and verification commands.

output_examples.input: A refactor proposal for moving validation into a shared service.
output_examples.output: A task-by-task migration plan that starts with tests, changes one component at a time, and ends with documented checks.

output_examples.input: A request to prepare work for another AI coding session.
output_examples.output: A handoff-ready plan that lists implementation tasks and offers subagent-driven or parallel-session execution choices.

best_practices: Provide the completed design, target files, and any repository conventions before using the skill.
Review suggested commands and file paths before running any generated plan.
Keep each task small enough to test, verify, and commit independently.
anti_patterns: Using the skill before the product or technical design is clear.
Treating generated commands as approved for execution without review.
Combining many unrelated features into one implementation plan.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces detailed implementation plans with goals, architecture notes, tasks, files, tests, commands, and handoff choices.

faq.question: Does it write production code directly?
faq.answer: No. It creates a plan that can guide a later implementation session.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a completed design, feature goal, repository context, constraints, and known testing expectations.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It may include example commands in a plan, but execution requires separate user or agent action.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-code projects?
faq.answer: It is designed for software implementation plans and may be less useful for non-code planning.
